title: Weak SSH daemon setting ({fw}) — review required
description: sshd weakens authentication or session controls: {sink} ({fw}). Empty passwords, disabled PAM, forwarding, and lax limits widen remote access. This lexical rule flags the setting; the reviewer hardens via {safe}.
limitation: Lexical, line-based: matches the setting regardless of Match blocks.
scopeT: Single-line lexical match on sshd settings.
fp: Bastion-specific needs are the rare accepted case.
recordDesc: For {fw}, {sink} weakens SSH authentication or session limits, so empty passwords, disabled PAM or broad forwarding widen remote access. The remedy is the hardened directive ({safe}).
verifyT: Rescan shows no weak setting; sshd -T confirms.

title: Open FTP setting ({fw}) — review required
description: FTP grants anonymous or write access: {sink} ({fw}). Anonymous upload turns the server into a drop box. This lexical rule flags the setting; the reviewer restricts via {safe}.
scopeT: Single-line lexical match on FTP settings.
fp: Public mirrors are the common accepted case.
recordDesc: For {fw}, {sink} allows anonymous or writable FTP access, so the service can be used to read files or to host content for others. The remedy is to disable anonymous access and restrict write scope ({safe}).
risk: Anonymous access or upload; MEDIUM severity.

title: Guest share access ({fw}) — review required
description: Samba admits guests: {sink} ({fw}). Guest shares expose files to anyone on the network. This lexical rule flags the setting; the reviewer restricts via {safe}.
scopeT: Single-line lexical match on Samba settings.
fp: Public drop shares are the rare accepted case.
recordDesc: For {fw}, {sink} admits guest users to a share, so anyone who can reach the service reads the exported files without credentials. The remedy is authenticated access with a defined group ({safe}).

title: Dangerous NFS export ({fw}) — review required
description: NFS exports grant world write or root ({fw}): {sink}. no_root_squash lets remote root act as local root. This lexical rule flags the export; the reviewer restricts via {safe}.
limitation: Lexical, line-based: matches the export option.
scopeT: Single-line lexical match on NFS exports.
fp: Trusted clusters are the rare accepted case.
recordDesc: For {fw}, {sink} exports a path to the world or with root preserved, so remote clients can write files or act as local root. The remedy is a narrow client list with root squashing ({safe}).
risk: Remote root file access; HIGH severity.

title: Open DNS resolver ({fw}) — review required
description: DNS answers the world: {sink} ({fw}). Open recursion fuels amplification attacks. This lexical rule flags the setting; the reviewer scopes via {safe}.
scopeT: Single-line lexical match on DNS settings.
fp: Public resolvers are the rare accepted case.
recordDesc: For {fw}, {sink} opens recursion. The remedy is {safe}.

title: Authentication bypass ({fw}) — review required
description: Authentication is bypassed: {sink} ({fw}). Permit modules, no-auth sudo, and environment-preserving sudo grant access without proof. This lexical rule flags the entry; the reviewer removes it via {safe}.
scopeT: Single-line lexical match on auth configuration.
fp: Recovery consoles are the rare accepted case.
recordDesc: With {sink}, {fw} admits a user without proof of identity, through a permissive PAM module, passwordless sudo or an inherited environment. The remedy is to remove the entry and require authentication ({safe}).

cweDef.name: Insufficient Session Expiration
cweDef.summary: Credentials that never expire stay valid long after they should be rotated.

title: Password never expires ({lang}) — review required
description: Passwords effectively never expire: {sink}. Stale credentials stay valid indefinitely. This lexical rule flags the setting; the reviewer bounds via {safe}.
fp: Service accounts with rotation elsewhere are the accepted case.
recordDesc: With {sink}, passwords never age out. The remedy is {safe}.
verifyT: Rescan shows a bounded max age.

title: Weak proxy or service setting ({fw}) — review required
description: A service weakens transport or trust: {sink} ({fw}). Disabled TLS, skipped verification, and default credentials expose traffic and control. This lexical rule flags the setting; the reviewer hardens via {safe}.
scopeT: Single-line lexical match on service settings.
fp: Lab hosts are the common false positive.
recordDesc: For {fw}, {sink} disables transport security, skips certificate checks or keeps default credentials, so traffic and control become readable. The remedy is to restore verification and rotate the credential ({safe}).

caddy:tls.recordDesc: tls off serves the site over plain HTTP only, so the certificate, HSTS and the encrypted transport that Caddy would manage are all absent.
caddy:tls.risk: Anyone on the path reads and rewrites the traffic, including cookies and form posts; MEDIUM.

istio:disable.recordDesc: mode: DISABLE turns off mutual TLS between workloads, so sidecars forward traffic without presenting or checking a peer certificate.
istio:disable.risk: A workload on the network impersonates another service because no peer certificate is checked; MEDIUM.

consul:verify.recordDesc: verify_incoming = false makes Consul accept TLS connections from clients that present no certificate.
consul:verify.risk: Any host that reaches the agent port reads and changes the service catalogue; MEDIUM.

vault:mlock.recordDesc: disable_mlock = true tells Vault not to lock its memory pages, so the kernel may write unsealed key material to swap.
vault:mlock.risk: Encryption keys and unsealed secrets can land in swap or a core dump that outlives the process; MEDIUM.

minio:default.recordDesc: MINIO_ROOT_PASSWORD=minioadmin ships the vendor's published default root password.
minio:default.risk: Anyone who reaches the console with the published default owns the object store; MEDIUM.

slapd:rootpw.recordDesc: rootpw writes the directory root password into slapd.conf in clear form instead of referring to a hashed credential managed elsewhere.
slapd:rootpw.risk: Anyone who reads the configuration authenticates as the directory administrator; MEDIUM.

postfix:tlsonly.recordDesc: smtpd_tls_auth_only = no lets clients present SMTP credentials before STARTTLS completes, so authentication can happen on the plaintext phase.
postfix:tlsonly.risk: A network attacker captures or relays the SMTP credentials of every client; MEDIUM.

title: Privileged Compose service ({fw}) — review required
description: Compose grants host-level access: {sink} ({fw}). Privileged mode, host namespaces, and root mounts erase container isolation. This lexical rule flags the grant; the reviewer removes it via {safe}.
scopeT: Single-line lexical match on Compose files.
fp: Node agents are the rare accepted case.
recordDesc: With {sink}, {fw} gives a container host-level access through privileged mode, host namespaces or a root filesystem mount, which removes the isolation boundary. The remedy is the least-privilege form ({safe}).

title: Permissive Kubernetes pod ({fw}) — review required
description: Kubernetes grants host or root power: {sink} ({fw}). Host namespaces, root users, writable roots, and privilege escalation erase pod isolation. This lexical rule flags the grant; the reviewer removes it via {safe}.
scopeT: Single-line lexical match on Kubernetes manifests.
fp: Node agents are the rare accepted case.
recordDesc: With {sink}, {fw} grants a pod host resources, root identity, a writable root filesystem or privilege escalation, so a compromised container reaches the node. The remedy is the restricted form ({safe}).
risk: Cluster or host compromise; HIGH severity.

title: Weak Terraform setting ({fw}) — review required
description: Terraform weakens protection: {sink} ({fw}). Ignored drift, local execution, skipped snapshots, public databases, and cleartext secrets widen blast radius. This lexical rule flags the setting; the reviewer hardens via {safe}.
scopeT: Single-line lexical match on Terraform files.
fp: Ephemeral environments are the common accepted case.
recordDesc: With {sink}, {fw} weakens protection. The remedy is {safe}.

hcl:ignoreall.recordDesc: ignore_changes = all removes every resource attribute from drift detection, so later plans treat real infrastructure changes as intended.
hcl:ignoreall.risk: Out-of-band changes to access rules or encryption stay invisible when the next plan runs; MEDIUM.

hcl:localexec.recordDesc: provisioner "local-exec" runs a shell command on the machine that runs Terraform.
hcl:localexec.risk: Anyone who can change the configuration or its variables runs commands with the operator's credentials; MEDIUM.

hcl:authread.recordDesc: acl = "authenticated-read" grants read access to every AWS-authenticated account.
hcl:authread.risk: Any AWS customer who learns the object name reads it; MEDIUM.

hcl:forcedestroy.recordDesc: force_destroy = true lets a destroy plan delete a bucket that still holds objects.
hcl:forcedestroy.risk: One mistaken apply removes the bucket and its objects, including copies kept only there; MEDIUM.

hcl:nobackup.recordDesc: backup_retention_period = 0 turns off automated backups and point-in-time recovery for the database instance.
hcl:nobackup.risk: A bad write or a deleted instance leaves no point-in-time copy to restore; MEDIUM.

hcl:masterpw.recordDesc: master_password is written as a literal string in the configuration, so the highest-privilege database credential is stored with the code.
hcl:masterpw.risk: The database master credential is stored beside the code and in the state file; MEDIUM.

hcl:pg9.recordDesc: engine_version pins a database engine line that is past end of life, so the instance stops receiving engine security patches.
hcl:pg9.risk: The instance stops receiving security fixes, so known engine flaws stay unpatched; MEDIUM.

title: Risky GitHub Actions step ({fw}) — review required
description: A workflow takes a risky shortcut: {sink} ({fw}). Mutable action refs, broad tokens, deprecated commands, and self-hosted runners widen supply-chain impact. This lexical rule flags the step; the reviewer hardens via {safe}.
scopeT: Single-line lexical match on workflow files.
fp: Trusted first-party actions are the common accepted case.
recordDesc: With {sink}, {fw} runs a workflow step with mutable action references, broad tokens, deprecated commands or a self-hosted runner, which widens supply-chain impact. The remedy is the pinned, least-privilege form ({safe}).

title: Risky GitLab job ({fw}) — review required
description: A GitLab job keeps artifacts forever or runs on a shell executor: {sink} ({fw}). Eternal artifacts leak data; shell executors share the host. This lexical rule flags the job; the reviewer hardens via {safe}.
limitation: Lexical, line-based: matches the job setting.
scopeT: Single-line lexical match on pipeline files.
fp: Release artifacts are the common accepted case.
recordDesc: With {sink}, {fw} keeps artifacts indefinitely or runs jobs on a shell executor, so build output leaks over time or shares the host. The remedy is bounded retention and an isolated executor ({safe}).
risk: Data leak or host sharing; LOW severity.

title: Django security setting off ({fw}) — review required
description: Django disables a security control: {sink} ({fw}). Insecure cookies, no HTTPS redirect, no HSTS, and MD5 hashing weaken the app. This lexical rule flags the setting; the reviewer enables via {safe}.
scopeT: Single-line lexical match on Django settings.
fp: Local development is the common false positive.
recordDesc: With {sink}, {fw} controls are off. The remedy is {safe}.

python:djsess.recordDesc: SESSION_COOKIE_SECURE = False lets Django send the session cookie over plain HTTP.
python:djsess.risk: A network attacker who captures the session cookie replays it and acts as that user; MEDIUM severity because a request over HTTP has to happen first.

python:djcsrf.recordDesc: CSRF_COOKIE_SECURE = False lets Django send the CSRF cookie over plain HTTP, so the anti-forgery token is no longer tied to a TLS session.
python:djcsrf.risk: An observer of the CSRF token can pair it with a forged cross-site request, weakening the check that stops unwanted state changes; MEDIUM severity.

python:djssl.recordDesc: SECURE_SSL_REDIRECT = False stops Django redirecting plain HTTP requests to HTTPS.
python:djssl.risk: Users and API clients can complete a session in cleartext, so credentials and data are exposed on the first request; MEDIUM severity.

python:djhsts.recordDesc: SECURE_HSTS_SECONDS = 0 disables the Strict-Transport-Security header Django would send.
python:djhsts.risk: Without HSTS a browser can be downgraded to HTTP on a later visit, so interception stays possible even after TLS is restored; MEDIUM severity.

python:djmd5.recordDesc: MD5PasswordHasher stores new passwords as unsalted and deliberately fast MD5 digests.
python:djmd5.risk: A database read yields hashes that commodity hardware cracks at high rate, so the passwords leak beyond the breached site; MEDIUM severity.

title: Rails protection weakened ({fw}) — review required
description: Rails weakens a protection: {sink} ({fw}). Local-request errors leak internals, skipped forgery checks invite CSRF. This lexical rule flags the setting; the reviewer restores via {safe}.
scopeT: Single-line lexical match on Rails config.
fp: Development config is the common false positive.
recordDesc: With {sink}, {fw} protections weaken. The remedy is {safe}.

ruby:forgexcept.recordDesc: protect_from_forgery except: :create removes CSRF verification from the named action.
ruby:forgexcept.risk: A third-party page can submit the exempted action with the victim session, so the state change happens without the user intent; MEDIUM severity.

ruby:skipverify.recordDesc: skip_before_action :verify_authenticity_token disables Rails CSRF verification for the actions it applies to.
ruby:skipverify.risk: Any cross-site form or fetch carrying the session cookie reaches the action with no token check; MEDIUM severity.

title: Risky Express setting ({fw}) — review required
description: Express trusts broadly: {sink} ({fw}). Served dotfiles leak secrets; trusted proxies let clients spoof addresses. This lexical rule flags the setting; the reviewer narrows via {safe}.
scopeT: Single-line lexical match on Express config.
fp: Internal apps are the common accepted case.
recordDesc: With {sink}, {fw} accepts a setting that widens what the server exposes or trusts, so served dotfiles leak secrets and trusted proxies let clients spoof their address. The remedy is the restrictive setting ({safe}).

title: Risky Spring setting ({fw}) — review required
description: Spring exposes internals: {sink} ({fw}). Disabled SSL, open management, verbose health, and the H2 console widen access. This lexical rule flags the setting; the reviewer restricts via {safe}.
scopeT: Single-line lexical match on Spring config.
fp: Local development is the common false positive.
recordDesc: With {sink}, {fw} exposes internals. The remedy is {safe}.

properties:ssl.recordDesc: server.ssl.enabled=false starts the embedded container without a TLS connector, so every request and response on that port is plain HTTP.
properties:ssl.risk: Session cookies and credentials cross the network in clear text; MEDIUM.

properties:mgmt.recordDesc: management.security.enabled=false removes authentication from the management endpoints.
properties:mgmt.risk: Actuator endpoints answer unauthenticated callers, including env and shutdown where exposed; MEDIUM.

properties:health.recordDesc: endpoints.health.sensitive=false returns component detail without authentication.
properties:health.risk: Health output names backends, disk paths and versions that map the deployment; MEDIUM.

properties:h2.recordDesc: spring.h2.console.enabled=true publishes the H2 web console at /h2-console, a servlet that runs SQL entered in a browser form.
properties:h2.risk: The console runs arbitrary SQL against the application database whenever it is reachable; MEDIUM.

title: PHP session exposure ({fw}) — review required
description: PHP sessions travel insecurely: {sink} ({fw}). Cookies without Secure or HttpOnly leak over HTTP and to scripts; URL session ids leak through links. This lexical rule flags the setting; the reviewer hardens via {safe}.
fp: Local development is the common false positive.
recordDesc: With {sink}, {fw} sessions are exposed. The remedy is {safe}.
